title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Sept. 29
gist: A weekly roundup listing eight new chip research papers, spanning A7 CFET vs. A10 nanosheet transistors, wafer-scale sub-5nm MoS2 transistors, multi-kW power delivery for 3D integration, GPU Rowhammer attacks, RTL Trojan localization, HBM/host-memory LLM inference, and agent-driven HLS chip design.

insights.claim: TU Munich, the University of Modena and Reggio Emilia and Applied Materials published a system-technology co-evaluation of A7 CFET versus A10 nanosheet FET technologies, from cell parasitics to chip reliability.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
entities: University of Modena and Reggio Emilia
insights.so_what: Equipment makers like Applied Materials are actively researching the CFET transition beyond nanosheets.

insights.claim: Researchers from Carnegie Mellon, University of Florida, MIT and Texas A&M report wafer-scale 2D MoS2 transistors with sub-5nm channel length and subthreshold performance beyond the silicon limit.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: 2D-material channels at wafer scale are a potential long-run path past silicon scaling limits.
insights.quote: subthreshold performance beyond the silicon limit

insights.claim: University of Minnesota research addresses methodologies for multi-kW power delivery in advanced 3D heterogeneous integration.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Power delivery is becoming a gating problem for high-power 3D-integrated AI packages.

insights.claim: Purdue and UCLA present experimental evidence that copper microstructure affects residual stress in through-silicon vias.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: TSV reliability matters for HBM and 3D stacking yields.

insights.claim: University of Toronto's GPUThor paper shows Rowhammer attacks amplified via non-uniform patterns can exploit ECC-protected GPUs.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Highlights a security vulnerability class in GPU memory relevant to shared AI infrastructure.

insights.claim: University of Wisconsin-Madison and Marist University research examines gate-level localization of RTL hardware Trojans.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Hardware supply-chain trust tooling is an active research area.

insights.claim: Georgia Tech, Nvidia Research and Stanford propose BOOST, which accelerates LLM inference by concurrently accessing host memory and HBM.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Memory capacity/bandwidth for inference is pushing designs to tap host memory alongside HBM.

insights.claim: A UCLA paper asks whether AI agents can design better chips when working at a higher level of abstraction via high-level synthesis.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Agentic AI for chip design is a growing research and EDA theme.
insights.quote: Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?
